+## Why
+Decode is 12.6 ms/tok at 2k, 13.9 at 32k and 15.7 at 64k. Only the 8 full-attention visits grow with the context, so they cost ~3 ms per token at 64k. The Qwen work found gains by tuning the decode query grouping (#570, TurboFlash).
+
+## What
+- Microbenchmark `inkling2DecodeAttention` (the `groupedDecodeSplitSource` and `relativeDecodeReduceSource` paths) at 8k, 32k and 64k keys, across split counts and threadgroup sizes.
+- Choose the split by the key count.
+
+## Acceptance
+- [ ] inklingcheck.sh: CHECK PASS. The raw32768 golden covers the long path.
+- [ ] inklingbench.sh shows a gain at 32k and 64k beyond the noise, with no loss at 2k.
+- [ ] The decode attention kernel tests pass. #inkling-perf
\ No newline at end of file

 ## Why
-Decode is 12.6 ms/tok at 2k, 13.9 at 32k and 15.7 at 64k. Only the 8 full-attention visits grow with the context, so they cost ~3 ms per token at 64k. The Qwen work found gains by tuning the decode query grouping (#570, TurboFlash).
+The ^pxcccjs attribution: the decode attention kernel costs 1.55 ms/token at 2k and 2.90 at 32k, against bandwidth floors of ~0.35 and ~1.8 ms.
+- `inkling2DecodeAttention` runs the sliding visits (≤1024 keys, 40 of 48) as one threadgroup per query head: 24 threadgroups, while the M5 Ultra has many more cores.
+- The split path (full visits past 1024 keys) uses 256 keys per split, so it launches only 8×S/256 threadgroups.

 ## What
-- Microbenchmark `inkling2DecodeAttention` (the `groupedDecodeSplitSource` and `relativeDecodeReduceSource` paths) at 8k, 32k and 64k keys, across split counts and threadgroup sizes.

+- Microbenchmark first: set `singleThreadgroupDecodeKeys` and `keysPerSplit` (and the simdgroups) by env in a scratch build, and run inklingcli profile/bench at 2k and 32k.
+- Candidates:
+  - (a) Send sliding visits down the split path with small splits (64 or 128 keys), so there are ≥128 threadgroups.
+  - (b) Choose the split count by the key count, aiming at a fixed threadgroup count.
+- The verify rows (`causalRows`) share the function, so a verify pass keeps the bits of decode steps.

--- original

@@ -1,6 +1,23 @@

 assignees:
 - claude-code
+comments:
+- actor: claude-code
+  id: 01m8496a0x7n8q17s8kq2s2w14
+  text: |-
+    ## Result: no change. Reverted (scratchpad/inktune.patch keeps the env knobs)
+    I microbenchmarked `inkling2DecodeAttention` (inklingcli `attn`) at real shapes with fresh K/V per call, 8 calls per eval, and a second repetition to warm up:
+    - Full layers at S ≥ 4k run at memory bandwidth whatever the split: 64k takes 279 us per call for 268 MB, ~960 GB/s; 131k takes 519 us. The splits I tried (8×256, 8×512, 8×1024, 16×1024, 4×128) all land within ±2%. The apparent 32k win in the first pass was warm-up noise.
+    - S=1024 (sliding) costs ~20 us per call and S=128 costs ~14 us, against a 4.4 us floor. The relative bias is not the cause: DR=1 or R=16 changes nothing. The cost is fixed per call, and most of it is CPU, see below.
+
+    ## The real finding: decode is CPU-bound
+    - **xctrace Metal System Trace of `bench` (ctx 2k, 256 tokens):** the GPU is busy 68.7% of decode. About once per token it waits ~4 ms. That is ~8.7 ms of GPU work per token, against the 12.6 ms/token observed.
+    - **Time Profiler, main thread:** TokenIterator.next splits into async_eval (encode, ~35% of all samples) and the Swift graph build (~25%).
+    - **Custom kernels cost ~42% of the main thread.** The build side is `MLXFastKernel.callAsFunction` → `mlx_fast_metal_kernel_apply` (12%): `write_signature` rebuilds the whole kernel source string on every call (memmove, malloc and free). The encode side is `CustomKernel::eval_gpu` (19%): it hashes the whole source (`std::hash`) and runs `fmt::format` on the library name for each dispatch, plus the dispatch itself.
+    - This is upstream mlx (mlx-swift 0.33.0, `backend/common/metal_kernel.cpp` and `backend/metal/custom_kernel.cpp`). Inkling makes ~430 custom-kernel calls per token.
+
+    Next: a new top card for compiled decode segments, the Qwen lesson, which replays built primitives and skips the Swift build and the source rebuild. A second card for an upstream mlx patch: cache the generated source per template, and cache the library name per CustomKernel.
+  timestamp: 2026-11-23T13:23:11.517458+00:00
